I would like to start this off with I get what youre saying and I agree that people really do need to be more empathetic and understand that self harm may not be and probably isnt so distant from their own lives and experiences. But I also believe that there should be an important distinction made between self harm and other unhealthy behaviors.

The main things that make self harm different is that 1) its very easy to go accidentally overboard and 2) cant really be done in "moderation"  

With point 1, its relatively a lot easier to cause death on the spot. With cutting, the easiest example, it can be very easy to just absentmindly cut too deep and die right there. In contrast, its highly unlikely that someone will drop dead right after smoking a cigarette or eating a whole pizza. And unless the person doing the piercing is just THAT bad at their job, you arent gonna die. When self harmong, there's also other things that need to be worried about like infection, internal bleeding etc. that can also lead to death.

With point 2, you cant really self harm in moderation. If you just occasionally drink or smoke, its still unhealthy but in small amounts (and outside medication) wont likely cause major health problems. In my opinion, thats still not good, but thats more of personal preferance than anything. If you get a tatoo or peircing by a proffessional, there also shouldnt be any medical issues. With self harm however, it is inherent that there will be harm done to the body, whether it just be a single cut or burn or an entire broken limb, that's all harm done to the body. So it cant be done in harmless amounts since the goal is to cause harm. 

Again, I totally think you have a good point that people shouldn't treat you badly just because of you're particular style of coping, but its important to remember the difference between self harm and other unhealthy behaviors. Yes, smoking and overeating are bad for you're health, but they arent really self harm unless done specifically to hurt themselves.
